% Invented deck whose title page declares a ground of its own and its own
% arrangement: the case a theme spells as a full-bleed fill over the page
% with each datum pinned to a point of it, written in the engine's own
% vocabulary. The pair is dark ground with light ink, declared — so the
% contrast judge tests the author's own pair and realizes nothing — and the
% frames after it keep the document's ground, which is what makes the
% declaration a page's and not a document's. The shape is a common theme
% construct; every colour, name and length is invented.
\documentclass[aspectratio=169]{slides}

\fonts{
  dir = "fonts",
  body = "Open Sans",
}

\palette{
  titlepagebg = #101822,
  titlepagefg = #F4F6F8,
}

\style{titlepage}{
  separator = none,
  slot = { set = title, anchor = west, at = west, xshift = 1.6cm, yshift = -0.4cm,
           width = 11cm, size = 18pt, align = left, font = {\bfseries} },
  slot = { set = subtitle, anchor = north west, at = north west, xshift = 1.6cm,
           yshift = -1.4cm, align = left },
  slot = { set = author, anchor = south west, at = south west, xshift = 1.6cm,
           yshift = 1.4cm, align = left, font = {\large} },
  slot = { set = institute, anchor = south east, at = south east, xshift = -1.6cm,
           yshift = 1.4cm, align = right },
  slot = { set = date, anchor = north east, at = north east, xshift = -1.6cm,
           yshift = -1.4cm, align = right },
}

\title{A Placeholder Deck}
\subtitle{Invented matter only}
\author{P. Placeholder}
\institute{example.org}
\date{2026-01-01}

\begin{document}

\maketitle

\begin{frame}{On the document's ground}
  Plain body text, on the ground every other page carries.
\end{frame}

\end{document}
